'''Joseph Pierre LaSalle''' (born 28 May 1916 in [[State College, Pennsylvania]]; died 7 July 1983 in [[Little Compton, Rhode Island]]) was an American mathematician specialising in [[dynamical systems]] and responsible for important contributions to [[stability theory]], such as [[LaSalle's invariance principle]] which bears his name.

==Biography==
Joseph LaSalle defended his [[Ph.D.]] thesis on ″''Pseudo-Normed Linear Sets over Valued Rings''″ at the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1941.<ref name=genealogy>[http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=10373 J. P. LaSalle on the Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref>
In 1946 he joined the Mathematics Department at the [[University of Notre Dame]] as an [[assistant professor]] and remained there until 1958, becoming a [[full professor]] in 1956.<ref name=inmemoriam>[http://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/0321049 SIAM J. Control Optim., 21(6), vii–ix. In Memoriam]</ref>
During a visit to [[Princeton University|Princeton]] in 1947–1948, LaSalle developed a deep interest in [[differential equation]]s through his interaction with [[Solomon Lefschetz]] and [[Richard Bellman]], with whom he developed a close friendship.<ref name=inmemoriam/> From 1958 until 1964 LaSalle was based at the [[Research Institute for Advanced Studies]] (RIAS) in [[Baltimore, Maryland|Baltimore]], where he worked closely with [[Solomon Lefschetz|Lefschetz]] and in 1960 published his extension of Lyapunov stability theory,<ref name=lasalleinv>{{cite journal
 |last         = LaSalle
 |first        = J. P.
 |date         = Dec 1960
 |title        = Some extensions of Liapunov's second method
 |url          = http://www.math.psu.edu/treluga/511/LaSalle1960.pdf
 |journal      = [[IRE Transactions on Circuit Theory ]]
 |publisher    = [[IEEE]]
 |volume       = 7
 |issue        = 4
 |pages        = 520–527
 |bibcode      = 1960IRTCT...7..520L
 |doi          = 10.1109/TCT.1960.1086720
 |access-date  = 2016-07-04
 |archive-date = 2019-04-30
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20190430182452/http://www.math.psu.edu/treluga/511/LaSalle1960.pdf
 |url-status   = dead
}}</ref> known today as [[LaSalle's invariance principle]].<ref name=inmemoriam/>

In 1962-1963 he was President of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM)<ref>[https://www.siam.org/about/more/presidents.php Presidents of SIAM]</ref> and was a member of its board of trustees in 1964–1967.<ref name=inmemoriam/> In 1964 LaSalle founded the [[Journal of Differential Equations]]<ref name=JDE>[http://www.journals.elsevier.com/journal-of-differential-equations/editorial-board/ Journal of Differential Equations Editorial Board]</ref> and served as its Editor-in-Chief until 1980.<ref name=inmemoriam/>
In 1964 he became the first director of the Center for Dynamical Systems at [[Brown University]], where he was also the chairman of the Division of Applied Mathematics in 1968–1973.<ref>[https://www.brown.edu/research/projects/dynamical-systems/about-us Center for Dynamical Systems at Brown University]</ref>

Together with [[Jack K. Hale|J. K. Hale]], LaSalle was the recipient of the 1965 [[Chauvenet Prize]] for their article, ″''Differential Equations: Linearity vs. Nonlinearity''″,<ref name=lasallehale>{{cite journal
 |last1        = LaSalle
 |first1       = Joseph P.
 |last2        = Hale
 |first2       = Jack K.
 |authorlink2  = Jack K. Hale
 |date         = July 1963
 |title        = Differential Equations: Linearity vs. Nonlinearity
 |url          = http://www.maa.org/sites/default/files/pdf/upload_library/22/Chauvenet/HaleLaSalleJoseph.pdf
 |journal      = [[SIAM Review]]
 |publisher    = SIAM
 |volume       = 5
 |issue        = 3
 |pages        = 249–272
 |bibcode      = 1963SIAMR...5..249H
 |doi          = 10.1137/1005068
 |access-date  = 2016-07-04
 |archive-date = 2015-10-04
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20151004015501/http://www.maa.org/sites/default/files/pdf/upload_library/22/Chauvenet/HaleLaSalleJoseph.pdf
 |url-status   = dead
}}</ref> published in the [[SIAM Review]].<ref name=chauvenet>{{Cite web |url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/chauvenet-prizes |title=Mathematical Association of America, Chauvenet Prize recipients |access-date=2015-08-27 |archive-date=2017-06-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628175100/http://maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/chauvenet-prizes |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1975 he was awarded the [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] for [[applied mathematics]].<ref name=guggenheim>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/joseph-p-lasalle/ Joseph P. LaSalle Guggenheim Fellowship, 1975]</ref>
